claim: The use of excessive force by officers negates probable cause for a lawful arrest under § 148(a)(1) only when the excessive force precedes any refusal to comply with ejection, and where such temporal ambiguity exists, individual officers cannot invoke qualified immunity unless it is clearly established that the violation of § 148(a)(1) was completed prior to the application of force.
initial_reasoning: 388 F. Supp. 3d 1158 discusses qualified immunity in the context of excessive force but does not limit the negation of probable cause to the specific temporal sequence described in the claim, nor does it require that the violation of § 148(a)(1) be completed before force is applied. The case does not establish the precise “temporal ambiguity” or the requirement that officers cannot invoke qualified immunity under those conditions.
